question: Which of the following causes of malabsorption occurs with alteration of the intestinal mucosa ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Celiac disease" -> "gluten ingestion" -> "immune response" -> "damage to intestinal mucosa" -> "malabsorption" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Crigler-Najjar syndrome" -> "bilirubin metabolism issue" -> "jaundice" -> "no direct effect on intestinal mucosa" -> "unlikely cause of malabsorption" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Cholestasis" -> "bile flow obstruction" -> "impaired fat digestion" -> "malabsorption of fat" -> "no direct alteration of intestinal mucosa" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Achalasia" -> "esophageal motility disorder" -> "difficulty swallowing" -> "no direct effect on intestinal mucosa" -> "unlikely cause of malabsorption" -> 30%
analysis: Celiac disease is a condition that leads to malabsorption due to damage and alteration of the intestinal mucosa. It is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to inflammation and damage to the villi in the small intestine, impairing nutrient absorption. The other options do not primarily involve alteration of the intestinal mucosa as a cause of malabsorption.
